claims.claim: Rollup sdiqt-1 created by the operator: nft profile, based sequencing, qledger-v1 execution, 10,000 QOR stake
Operator bonded 1,000 QOR as the sdiqt-1 batch submitter
Operator registered its ML-DSA-87 key; every operator tx is hybrid signed
Watchtower registered the ML-DSA-87 key that signs settlement receipts
Watchtower registered an ML-KEM-1024 key, the recipient of sealed exit packets
Demo user registered its ML-DSA-87 key before depositing
Demo user posted a signed qledger withdrawal of 2 QOR from L2-A to its L1 address (batch 3, proven by STARK)
After batch 3 was final, MsgExecuteWithdrawal paid 2 QOR to the demo user with the withdrawal's Merkle path
The watchtower opened the demo user's ML-KEM-1024 sealed exit packet at its release height and posted the 2.5 QOR withdrawal from L2-A to the inbox (batch 5, proven by STARK)
After batch 5 was final, MsgExecuteWithdrawal paid the sealed exit's 2.5 QOR to the demo user
The operator submitted batch 12 on purpose with the last byte of its state root flipped (gate G3, armed by a typed confirmation)

An independent challenger's qledger fraud proof rejected the staged batch 12 seven seconds after it landed; the chain slashed the operator's 1,000 QOR bond (500 burned, 500 to the challenger) and rolled the inbox back
The operator bonded 1,000 QOR again and resubmitted batch 12 with the correct root

open.plan: our watchtower's own MsgChallengeBatch on diana; in the staged run (batch 12) an independent challenger reached the chain 7 s after the submit, and our tower, polling every 30 s, recorded the rejection and the root mismatch in its receipt
